subject: general
question: A wholesaler offers a bulk order deal where a 10% discount is applied to orders above Rs. 15,000, and a 5% additional seasonal discount is available. What is the effective price paid for an order worth Rs. 20,000?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount multiplying factor method:

Effective Price = Original Price × (1 − D₁%) × (1 − D₂%)

⇒ Final Price = 20000 × 0.90 × 0.95

⇒ Final Price = 17100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 17,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original order value = Rs. 20,000

Since the order is above Rs. 15,000, the bulk discount of 10% applies.

Additional seasonal discount = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 
• 
• 
 
 −10% Discount −5% Discount 20k 18k 17.1k Original Price Intermediate Final Price Rs. 20000 Rs. 18000 Rs. 17100 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Apply the 10% bulk discount on Rs. 20,000

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 20000 − (10 ÷ 100 × 20000)

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 20000 − 2000 = Rs. 18,000

⇒ Step 2: Apply the 5% additional seasonal discount on the new intermediate price

⇒ Final Price = 18000 − (5 ÷ 100 × 18000)

⇒ Final Price = 18000 − 900 = Rs. 17,100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 17,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts Formula

When two discounts D₁% and D₂% are applied consecutively, the single equivalent effective discount is given by: D = D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂ ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The final amount paid by the customer is the Selling Price (SP), where SP = MP − Total Discount.
